files.content:
# Private pyproject metadata inspector

Python 3.11+ standard library only. Pipe a supplied pyproject.toml to app.py; --help or empty stdin prints instructions. Produces JSON with declared project name, version, requires-python, dependency count/list and script names. Missing version/requires-python remain null, never fabricated. Does not install, resolve dependencies, import project code, validate packaging standards or prove package safety. Input may contain private metadata: output is local only.

Hypothetical example: printf '[project]\nname="demo"\nversion="1.0"\n' | python3 app.py

import unittest
from app import inspect_project

class MetadataTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_missing_optional_values_are_unknown(self):
        result = inspect_project('[project]\nname="hypothetical-minimal"\n')
        self.assertIsNone(result['version'])
        self.assertIsNone(result['requires_python'])
        self.assertEqual(result['dependency_count'], 0)
    def test_real_computation(self):
        result = inspect_project('[project]\nname="hypothetical-demo"\ndependencies=["z>=1", "a"]\n[project.scripts]\ndemo="demo:main"\n')
        self.assertEqual(result['dependencies'], ['a', 'z>=1'])
        self.assertEqual(result['dependency_count'], 2)
        self.assertEqual(result['scripts'], ['demo'])
    def test_bad_inputs(self):
        for text in ('invalid[', '[tool.demo]\nx=1', '[project]\nname=7', '[project]\nname="demo"\ndependencies=[1]', '[project]\nname="demo"\nversion=1'):
            with self.subTest(text=text), self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                inspect_project(text)
